item.title: Undefeated UFC fighter found unresponsive in nightclub bathroom, rushed to nearby hospital
item.description: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 12: Tommy McMillen reacts after his victory over Marwan Rahiki of Morocco in their featherweight fight during the Noche UFC event at Desert Diamond Arena on September 12, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Tommy McMillen suffered the first knockout of his career — but it wasn’t inside the cage. The undefeated featherweight was found unresponsive inside the bathroom of Cake nightclub in Scottsdale, Arizona. Responding officers administered Narcan to counteract what they believed to be an accidental overdose, then had McMillen transported to a nearby hospital. TMZ first reported the news on Thursday. After making a splash on Dana White’s “Contender Series” back in late 2025, the Phoenix native jumped out to a 3-0 start under the UFC banner with two knockouts, pushing his overall record to 12-0 with 10 finishes. He was not booked to compete at the time of the incident, having fought as recently as September . McMillen, 28, is expected to make a full recovery though I’m sure this recent incident — which is sadly not uncommon among UFC fighters — is likely to hurt his good standing with UFC matchmakers for his inevitable return to action in early 2027.

item.title: The Washington Nationals cannot rely on Jake Irvin as a starting pitcher next season
item.description: WASHINGTON, DC - SEPTEMBER 26: Jake Irvin #27 of the Washington Nationals watches A.J. Ewing #9 of the New York Mets three run home run in the seventh inning during a baseball game at Nationals Park on September 26, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images This morning, Spencer Nusbaum wrote about the state of the Nationals pitching staff entering 2027, and there was one thing that stood out. He said that Paul Toboni indicated Jake Irvin had “put himself in good position to compete for a rotation spot”. Given the way Irvin has pitched for the past 2.5 seasons, I find that to be discouraging. Also in The Athletic this AM: Rumblings on the Nats’ plans to improve their pitching next year, including details on an analytics department that they are becoming more confident in by the day: https://t.co/4wszWRh3kG — Spencer Nusbaum (@spencernusbaum_) November 12, 2026 Back in 2024, Jake Irvin had a solid season, carried by a great first half. He posted a 4.41 ERA in 187.2 innings with 2 fWAR. Those are solid back of the rotation numbers. However, things have fallen apart since then. In 2025, he posted a 5.70 ERA and this season he had a 5.48 earned run average. With lower velocity and home run struggles, things have not been pretty for Irvin. Given how bad things have been, I would be quite pessimistic about giving Irvin yet another year in the rotation. We have a very long sample size of Irvin not being effective now. Since the All-Star break of 2024, Jake Irvin has posted a 5.68 ERA in 358.1 innings. I get that the Nats trust their player development team, but running it back with Irvin in the rotation does not make much sense. In some ways, I get why people would like Irvin. He is a big, strong right hander who generates a ton of extension and throws from a low arm slot. By all accounts, he is a great guy and hard worker as well. I actually think he could have success in the bullpen because of the fact he has shown the ability to sit in the mid-90’s for short bursts. Lost in my coverage of Sunday's games was a very encouraging performance by Jake Irvin. Starting with a drastically lower arm slot, Irvin's fastball sustained its ride to push it to a plus offering. He also altered his slider to give it more loft. He is a name to follow! pic.twitter.com/RsOKuVQgmn — Thomas Nestico (@TJStats) March 30, 2026 A big reason why the Nats seem to have faith in Irvin is because they believe that with the right development, he can sit at 95 MPH deep into starts. That is what Nusbaum wrote in his piece. However, I am not as convinced about this. Velocity fluctuation has been a problem for years now with Irvin. Will the light just suddenly come on for a pitcher who is about to turn 30 years old? That is what the team seems to hope for. Right now, he is working in West Palm Beach trying to increase that velocity. I will have to see it to believe it though because Irvin has been trying to solve this velocity problem for years now.

The hope is that the potential returns of Patrick Kane and Bowen Byram will help stabilize things at both ends of the rink. Byram has been upgraded to day-to-day after missing the last 11 games with an upper-body injury. Regardless of who’s in the lineup, the Blackhawks need to turn things around quickly if they hope to be one of the last eight standing in the Western Conference come April.

item.title: Steelers mid-season awards: Rookie of the Year
item.description: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images This marks our final mid-season award for the Pittsburgh Steelers. Thus far, we have crowned Jaylen Warren as the team’s mid-season MVP and Offensive Player of the Year, while T.J. Watt was crowned as the Defensive Player of the Year. Our final award will be Rookie of the Year, taking both sides of the ball into consideration rather than splitting it into two separate awards. With that said, here is how our staff voted. Joey Bray – OT Max Iheanachor: Ever since Max Iheanachor made his first start in Week 3, the Steelers’ offensive line has shown massive improvement. The first-round pick has beaten the “project” allegations with exceptional play from his first start in the league. Iheanachor is going to be a huge piece of the Steelers offensive line for years to come. Austin Bechtold – WR Germie Bernard & S Robert Spears-Jennings: I couldn’t pick just one so decided to pick one on each side of the ball. Bernard has impressed and earned Aaron Rodgers’ trust, something close to impossible for rookie wide receivers to do. In eight games, Bernard owns 32 catches for 284 yards and one touchdown. He’s basically played six games after only a handful of snaps against Atlanta and only one catch against Cincinnati. Bernard has a more diverse route tree than DK Metcalf and I think is a better all-around receiver. The Steelers found a gem in the second round and no one is going to miss out on Makai Lemon. Robert Spears-Jennings has a serious case to win this award outright. The Steelers continue to rave about his ability and keep playing the defensive back after DeShon Elliott returned. He’s registered 20 tackles and his first career interception against Cleveland. Spears-Jennings is PFF’s fifth-highest-graded rookie (78.7) and the highest-graded rookie tackler (82.7) in football. The former seventh-round pick looks like a starter for years to come. Spears-Jennings has helped solidify a veteran, but very vulnerable secondary. Ryan Parish – OT Max Iheanachor: Another race with several valid options. Seventh-rounder Robert Spears-Jennings has a case, as does Germie Bernard and Daylen Everette. But as one of the lone voices that was celebrating getting Iheanachor over Makai Lemon on draft weekend, I’m thrilled that he’s playing so well. The Steelers’ offense was unquestionably and definitively improved beginning the week Iheanachor took over as starter and the line as a whole is now a strength of the team. That locks up the award in my book. Ryland Bickley – OT Max Iheanachor: This was the easiest choice for me. The Steelers’ offensive success this season can be traced back to the moment Iheanachor and Brock Hoffman were inserted into the right side of the offensive line. Has Iheanachor been perfect? Far from it, but I’m not sure where the Steelers offense would be right now without the rookie tackle. item.title: NFL rumors: Chiefs, 49ers made long-shot Garrett Wilson trade efforts with Jets that went nowhere
item.description: Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images NFL rumors: Chiefs, 49ers made long-shot Garrett Wilson trade efforts with Jets that went nowhere appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Garrett Wilson was one of the biggest names to watch ahead of the NFL trade deadline, but the New York Jets never appeared seriously interested in moving their star wide receiver. That didn’t stop two Super Bowl contenders from checking in. According to ESPN’s Rich Cimini, the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers were interested in acquiring Wilson. However, a trade was never a realistic possibility. Wilson didn’t want to leave New York, and the Jets had no desire to part ways with arguably their best player. Wilson is under contract through 2030 and remains a foundational piece of the organization’s future. Even with the Jets struggling, the front office clearly wasn’t interested in making another franchise-altering move by trading away its top offensive weapon. That doesn’t mean Wilson is completely satisfied with how things are going in New York. He recently made it clear that winning remains his biggest priority, even though he loves playing for the Jets. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I want to win games and that’s the one thing we’ve been missing here. I love it here. Do I love it more than I love winning? Nah, to be completely honest, but I’m hopeful,” Wilson said. Those comments are worth remembering as the offseason approaches. If the Jets continue struggling and Wilson becomes increasingly frustrated with the direction of the franchise, trade speculation could return. The Chiefs and 49ers certainly could have used a receiver of Wilson’s caliber. Kansas City ultimately acquired Josh Downs , while San Francisco landed veteran Keenan Allen . Both teams addressed their receiver needs, but neither managed to land the young star who could have dramatically changed its offense. For now, Wilson remains in New York. But if the Jets cannot convince him that their future is heading in the right direction, this storyline could become much more interesting during the offseason. item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. item.title: "He loves all people" – Klopp defends Nmecha after chat over controversial celebration
item.description: "He loves all people" – Klopp defends Nmecha after chat over controversial celebration After their personal discussion, Jürgen Klopp is of the opinion that Felix Nmecha holds no I'll feeling towards any member of society following his controversial crown celebration . “Yes, that was a major topic of discussion. Perhaps we should briefly go back,” he said at today's press conference, regarding Nmecha's celebration which was linked with a group that holds anti-LGBTQ+ beliefs. "I watched football last weekend and saw Felix score two wonderful goals. I also saw his goal celebration. First the celebration itself, and then the gesture, as we'll call it. "I honestly didn't think anything of it. Then all the discussions started. Perhaps that was down to my ignorance or whatever, but I didn't think anything of it initially. "Then, as the debate gathered pace, I started looking into it and trying to inform myself. It was clear to me that I would, of course, want to speak to Felix as soon as we met, because I consider that the most important thing “I've known Felix Nmecha for a few months now, I would say. He's an exceptionally friendly, warm and open young man who, whenever he's around us, radiates nothing but positive energy,” Klopp said. Regarding the interaction that would follow, Klopp revealed that it was difficult for him to approach. He was well aware of the traction it was getting in the media too. "I said to him: “Right, this is the situation, and this is what's being discussed as a result of it. What are we going to do about it? People are asking me what I should say.” "I then confronted him with everything that you would probably have confronted him with as well: what some people out there might think. To be clear, I'm not one of those people, but some people do think that way. "And he said: "It has absolutely nothing to do with that. He loves all people and doesn't discriminate against anyone." - For me, that settled the most important part of the matter. "Then I asked him: "What about the goal celebration? How are we going to handle that? Your message, as you've explained it to me, is a very positive one. But out there, it's being interpreted in a particular way. "So what do we do about that?" - He said: "Well, I won't do that anymore." And that's why he won't celebrate like that again. But let me reiterate: he wasn't trying to convey any message beyond his own personal one. “His message is that he lays the crown at Jesus' feet. That's all it means to him. There is no further message or hidden meaning behind it. And with that, I was satisfied,” Klopp summarized.

item.description: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 08: Daiyan Henley #0 of the Los Angeles Chargers reacts during the second quarter of a game against the Philadelphia Eagles at SoFi Stadium on December 08, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) Getty The reason for the Broncos and Chargers canceled Daiyan Henley trade has come to light. Getty Chargers LB Daiyan Henley Getty The Denver Broncos decided not to go through with the Daiyan Henley trade late Wednesday night, leaving the Los Angeles Chargers stuck in one of the most awkward spots in the league. After already saying goodbye to their starting linebacker and deleting the post, LA had to take him right back with a welcome-back post. Henley was more confused than the Chargers fans, and he wasted no time sharing that on social media. Daiyan Henley Reacts With Confused GIF Getty Daiyan Henley reacts to Broncos cancelling trade. “ Henley, shortly after news broke that the trade would not go through, posted a GIF on his X account depicting a man with a confused expression,” The Athletic’s Nick Kosmider reported. Neither team gave an official explanation for why the deal fell apart, though both franchises noted Tuesday that the trade was pending a physical. Both teams announced Tuesday before the 4 p.m. ET deadline that the deal was contingent on Henley passing a physical. Henley traveled to Denver on Wednesday to take his exam at the Broncos’ facility. As Kosmider noted, if Denver officially designated him as a failed physical, that designation will appear on Thursday’s NFL transaction wire. Multiple sources confirmed that Henley failing the exam was a reason behind the trade not falling through. NBC Sports’ Mike Florio also added to the report, saying Henley failed the physical. Multiple Reports Believe Daiyan Henley Failed the Physical Exams Getty Chargers LB Daiyan Henley “Per a source with knowledge of the situation, Henley did indeed fail the physical in Denver,” Florio wrote. “It was, we’re told, a knee issue. Although Henley appeared on the Week 9 injury report with a shoulder problem, he was listed with a knee injury in Week 6,” Florio wrote. “Every trade hinges on the passing of a physical. The player rarely fails it. Still, when he does, the trade doesn’t happen. The problem with eleventh-hour deadline deals that fall through is that the team that thought it was acquiring a new player now can’t pivot elsewhere.” Then Florio also explored the possibility of the Broncos getting cold feet after committing two late-round picks, citing the classic failed Maxx Crosby trade. “Of course, there’s always the possibility that the Broncos got cold feet after committing a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the transaction. item.title: Zay Flowers, Chig Okonkwo, And More Fantasy Football Buy-Low Trade Candidates For Week 10
item.description: Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers (4) speaks to the media after the game at Maracana Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It's not always easy to have foresight, but fantasy owners have to know when it's time to go after a struggling player and buy low on them. That is how you maximize value and build a championship team. These are the top fantasy football buy-low trade candidates for Week 10. Buy-Low Trade Candidates: Week 10 RB Chase Brown, Cincinnati Bengals Brown has been less than spectacular this season, but this has been the case for the past couple of seasons now, and then he explodes as we get into November. Everything has been in place for Brown to be the great fantasy football running back we've seen in the past, but the production just hasn't gotten there. As the weather gets colder in the AFC North, we start to see more running and short passes. This is when Brown takes off and becomes the RB1 he has become late in the year the past few seasons. His playoff schedule also features the Carolina Panthers, Indianapolis Colts, and Baltimore Ravens. This is a player you should be targeting. RB Derrick Henry, Baltimore Ravens There was a lot of fear surrounding Henry's fantasy value after Lamar Jackson went down for the remainder of the season. The addition of Jacoby Brissett helps negate that fear. While bringing in Brissett won't necessarily equate to victories, it should be enough to maintain the other fantasy weapons on the team. Henry will once again be the monster he always is late in the season when the weather gets cold, and the team needs to lean on him. WR Zay Flowers, Baltimore Ravens We go from Henry to Flowers, and this is a similar story, but even stronger for Flowers. If there is one thing that Brissett does as a starting quarterback, it's hyper-target "his guy". There is no reason to believe that Flowers won't be "his guy". With one trade for Brissett, Flowers went from a shaky flex option to potentially climbing back into the WR1 conversation. TE Chig Okonkwo, Washington Commanders Okonkwo was one of our top tight end sleepers leading into the season, but a Week 1 hamstring injury seemed to derail everything. However, it looks like he is getting back on track, and we expect him to be a low-end TE1 for the remainder of the season. You should be targeting him in trades now, and you can probably get him fairly cheaply. If you acquire him now, he will be a tight end whom you can start most weeks for the rest of the fantasy season. item.title: I managed Wrexham - Phil Parkinson needs to follow my lead to get best out of his team
item.description: Wrexham will face Lincoln City after the international break -Credit:GETTY Every manager will have a philosophy, a preferred way of playing and, ideally, a preferred starting eleven. But football has a habit of ripping up even the best-laid plans. Injuries, illness, loss of form, suspensions, attitude and a whole host of other factors can quickly turn a managers carefully constructed blueprint on its head. That is when flexibility, both tactically and within the squad, becomes so important. The past week has been a good example of how a relatively small tactical adjustment can make a significant difference, particularly when a squad is being ravaged by injuries in key attacking areas. With three creative players unavailable, alongside the new long-term injury to Sam Smith (wishing him a speedy recovery), Phil Parkinson has been forced to revisit a familiar formation from our League One campaign. Without our recognised ‘number 10s’, he has returned to a midfield three, with one holding midfielder, or ‘6’, and two more advanced ‘8s’, rather than the previous system of two deeper midfielders and two attacking tens. For me, it brought greater balance. Against Blackburn, Todd Cantwell had found plenty of joy drifting into the wide areas when we were playing with narrow deep midfielders, a number 10 and two strikers. The change helped provide greater defensive stability, but it also offered something going forward. The two ‘8s’ were given more licence to get beyond the ball, link up with the wing-backs and connect with the strikers. It gave us different options and, importantly, a better balance between attack and defence. • All the Phil Parkinson questions you wanted to know but were afraid to ask • Phil Parkinson may need to change his trusted approach to get Wrexham fans back on side Would that change have happened if everyone had been fit? Probably not. And that’s where management becomes interesting. There was another calculated gamble in moving Lewis O’Brien into the number 10 role, playing just off Kieffer Moore. It isn’t a natural position for Lewis, who generally prefers to operate from deeper areas, but he certainly possesses some of the attributes required. His energy allows him to lead the press, he anticipates situations well and his movement can cause opponents problems. It’s a risk when a player hasn’t regularly occupied that position, but Parkinson’s options are limited and sometimes necessity forces your hand. This is where a manager needs a little bit of creative thinking, and perhaps a slice of luck. A new combination clicks, a player discovers a position that suits him or somebody takes an unexpected opportunity and makes it their own. Of course, it doesn’t always work! Brian Flynn and Peter Reid both decided that playing me at right midfield might be the answer at various points in my career. Let’s just say those particular experiments weren’t quite as successful! Lewis O'Brien put in a brilliant performance in the No.10 role -Cred

Nonetheless, The Ringer’s NFL insider Tom Pelissero isn’t going that far with his outlook on Murray’s future in the league. “If Kyler wants to be in the NFL next season, he can be in the NFL, and he can still be a starting quarterback,” Pelissero said during a Nov. 12 appearance on KFAN . “This was an experiment by Kevin O’Connell. “He wanted to take a guy who’d never been coached this way, never played in exactly this style of offense, but had a really unique skill set for the position in terms of his mobility and his legs, and see if it worked out.
